plain.text: As Jacob went on his way, the angels of God met him. Jacob sent messengers to his brother Esau in Edom, saying he had been living with Laban and hoped to find favour. The messengers returned: Esau was coming to meet him with four hundred men. Jacob was greatly afraid and divided his people and flocks into two camps. He prayed, "O God of my father Abraham, I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown me. Save me from my brother Esau, for I am afraid. But you said, 'I will surely make you prosper.'" He sent large herds of goats, sheep, camels, cattle and donkeys ahead as a gift for Esau, in separate groups, hoping to calm his anger.

That night Jacob sent his family and possessions across the Jabbok River, and was left alone. A man wrestled with him until daybreak. When the man saw he could not overpower Jacob, he touched the socket of Jacob's hip, and it was wrenched. The man said, "Let me go, for it is daybreak." Jacob replied, "I will not let you go unless you bless me." "What is your name?" "Jacob." "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed." The man blessed him there. Jacob named the place Peniel ("face of God"), saying, "I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared." He limped as the sun rose.

summary.bigIdea: Afraid of meeting Esau, Jacob prays honestly and wrestles through the night, receiving a new name: Israel.
points: Jacob is terrified of Esau and prays, admitting he is unworthy.
Alone at night, he wrestles with a mysterious man until daybreak.
"I will not let you go unless you bless me": Jacob becomes Israel and leaves limping.
summary.reflection: Jacob held on to God and would not let go. What are you wrestling with God about?
